# fourthirtyfive

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/kuriwaki/fourthirtyfive/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kuriwaki/fourthirtyfive/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->


Maintainer: Shiro Kuriwaki

Contributors: Zoya Ahmer, Zachary Donnini, Cory McCartan

Copyright holders: Downballot (some data)


`fourthirtyfive` is a package that provides shapefiles and other data for the 435 congressional districts, gathering good ideas from various authors. The current data cover 2006-2025.

## Installation

You can install the development version of fourthirtyfive from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
remotes::install_github("kuriwaki/fourthirtyfive")
```


## Example

The main output of the package are datasets which comes pre-loaded with the package.

```{r example}
library(fourthirtyfive)
```


We are building several types of maps. First, the **dotmap** is where one CD is treated as point. We use the centroid of the actual map, and dodge it so that crowded points do not completely overlap with each other.

```{r}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

load_shp_dot(2023) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = shp_states) +
  geom_sf(size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_void()
```

For now, the output of each function for recent years is stored as a package dataset as well:

```{r}
shp_dot_2023
```


We also provide **hexmaps** (i.e., maps that present CDs as combinations of hexagons) for all years. The 2013-2025 maps are sourced from the Downballot's hex map shapefiles (<https://the-db.co/maps>). The 2005-2011 maps are generated with Cory McCartan's [hexmap](https://github.com/CoryMcCartan/hexmap) package.

```{r}
load_shp_hex(2023) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void() +
  labs(caption = "Map Source: https://the-db.co/maps")
```

Note: An earlier version of these hex maps was provided in the [`donnermap`](https://github.com/kuriwaki/donnermap) package. Those shapefiles used unprojected coordinates that do not match the coordinate system of the other hex maps here. The hex maps in `fourthirtyfive` use the projected Web Mercator versions (`wm` suffix) from the Downballot.



We do not store actual CD shapefiles, but we provide a function to draw these from either the Census or Jeff Lewis's historical shapefiles.

Use `load_cd_shps(year = 2027)` for the 120th Congress. The nine states redrawn for the 2026 election use Census's 2026 TIGER/Line boundaries, simplified together for plotting by default; all other states, including Missouri, retain the 2025 map. Use `simplify = FALSE` for full detail. The assembled 2027 map is cached within the R session; use `cache = FALSE` to rebuild it.

```{r, include = FALSE}
suppressMessages(cd_shps <- load_cd_shps(c = 118))
```

```{r, eval=FALSE}
cd_shps <- load_cd_shps(c = 118)
```

```{r}
cd_shps |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf() +
  theme_void()
```


We also provide a dataset of the **descriptive names** of each district (e.g., calling AZ-01 in the 110th congressional district "Phoenix exurbs, Prescott, and Flagstaff"). 
These use [Daily
Kos](https://www.dailykos.com/stories/2022/8/8/2113098/-The-Daily-Kos-Elections-naming-guide-to-this-decade-s-new-congressional-districts) namings. Zachary Donnini named 2008-2010 congressional districts.


```{r}
load_cd_info(2007)
```

This can be loaded as an object too, for now:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
info_2007
```



## Data format

We name the datasets (`shp_dot_**`, `info_**`) by the year of the congress.

|Object | Congress | Years in Session | Year Elected | Year up for Election | 
|-------|----------|-------|---------------|----------|
|`**_2005` | 109th | 2005-2006 | 2004 | 2006 |
|`**_2007` | 110th | 2007-2008 | 2006 | 2008 |
|`**_2009` | 111th | 2009-2010 | 2008 | 2010 |
|`**_2011` | 112th | 2011-2012 | 2010 | 2012 |
|`**_2013` | 113th | 2013-2014 | 2012 | 2014 | 
|`**_2015` | 114th | 2015-2016 | 2014 | 2016 |
|`**_2017` | 115th | 2017-2018 | 2016 | 2018 |
|`**_2019` | 116th | 2019-2020 | 2018 | 2020 |
|`**_2021` | 117th | 2021-2022 | 2020 | 2022 |
|`**_2023` | 118th | 2023-2024 | 2022 | 2024 |
|`**_2025` | 119th | 2025-2026 | 2024 | 2026 |
